name: Can an ADU bathroom be designed for aging in place?

mainEntity.name: What bathroom features make an ADU more usable for older adults or long-term occupants?
mainEntity.text: What bathroom features make an ADU more usable for older adults or long-term occupants?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU bathroom can be made much more usable for aging in place if the features are planned during construction. A curbless or low-threshold shower, wider turning clearances, reinforced walls for grab bars, slip-resistant flooring, and a comfort-height toilet are common upgrades that improve safety and accessibility. Good lighting and a simple, uncluttered layout also matter because they reduce trip hazards and make the room easier to use. If the ADU may later house parents, guests, or long-term tenants, these features can add meaningful value without making the bathroom feel institutional. The best time to include them is during design, since changing to a curbless shower or wider doorway after construction is much more expensive. Homeowners should talk to the builder about future needs even if the current occupant is younger, because ADUs are often used by different people over time. A well-planned bathroom can be both stylish and adaptable.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an ADU bathroom can be designed for aging in place with a curbless shower, wider clearances, grab bar backing, slip-resistant flooring, and a comfort-height toilet. Good lighting and a simple layout also help. These features should be built in during construction because retrofitting them later is more expensive.
